llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it says (fetch HN/RSS, classify items, generate reports) but the package metadata omits required binaries and environment variables and the runtime will send feed content to third‑party LLM endpoints if API keys are provided — review before installing or supplying keys.

dimensions.detail: The scripts and SKILL.md match the described purpose: fetching Hacker News submissions and RSS/OPML feeds, classifying items, and producing reports. However the registry metadata claims 'required binaries: none' and 'required env vars: none' while the README/SKILL and scripts expect bash, curl, python3 and jq (classify.sh checks for jq). That metadata omission is inconsistent and worth noting.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to run shipped bash scripts that read local OPML files or take a HN username, fetch remote data from Hacker News and arbitrary RSS URLs, classify items, and render a Markdown report. This stays within the declared feature set. Important: classification will be performed by either an on‑agent 'openclaw llm' invocation or by direct HTTP calls to Anthropic/OpenAI using any API keys present — meaning title/URL content will be transmitted to those third parties if keys are set.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec — it's an instruction + script bundle. Nothing downloads arbitrary code during install; code is run from the skill directory. This is lower install risk than fetching remote binaries, but the shipped scripts will perform network I/O at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata declares no required env vars, but SKILL.md and classify.sh make optional use of ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY (recommended for better classification). Those keys are proportionate to the stated LLM classification capability. Additional environment usage: FEED_DIET_BATCH_SIZE, XDG_CACHE_HOME (used to create ~/.cache/feed-diet). The metadata mismatch (declaring none while code optionally uses LLM keys) is inconsistent and should be corrected/understood before providing secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always: true and does not modify other skills or system configuration. It writes cache files to $XDG_CACHE_HOME or $HOME/.cache/feed-diet, which is expected for a CLI-style tool. It does not request elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to check before installing/using Feed Diet:

- Metadata mismatch: the registry claims no required binaries/env vars, but the scripts require bash, curl, python3 and jq. Ensure those are present and that you trust the author.
- Network & data flow: the tool fetches HN and arbitrary RSS feed URLs you provide and writes a cache under ~/.cache/feed-diet. That is expected, but be careful not to point it at feeds containing sensitive tokens or internal URLs.
- LLM classification: if you set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY (or if the local 'openclaw' CLI is present), the skill will send item titles/URLs (the content being analyzed) to the corresponding LLM provider. Don’t provide secrets or private content if you do not want that transmitted.
- Safety checks in the code: OPML feed URLs are limited to http/https (mitigates trivial SSRF). Good practice is still to run in a sandbox or inspect the scripts locally first.

Recommended actions:
1) Review the scripts yourself (they are included) and verify jq/curl/python3 usage. 2) Run on non-sensitive feeds or a small test OPML first. 3) If you do not want data sent to external LLMs, do NOT set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY and ensure 'openclaw' isn't available in PATH; the skill will then fall back to local keyword rules. 4) If you must supply an API key, consider creating a provider account/key with restricted/quota-limited access. 5) If anything is unclear, ask the author to update registry metadata to list binaries and optional env vars before installing.
